summary: Feed s120_double to NDR is degraded: VLAN 20 is completely missing (50% untagged) and 94.2% of bytes are encrypted exceeding the NDR's 90% tolerance. No duplicates, drops, overload or one-way issues detected.

findings.root_cause: 802.1Q tags are being stripped before the tool - ingress TAP/SPAN or packet broker port is in access mode or has VLAN stripping enabled, and trunk is not configured to preserve tags end-to-end. Result is 50% untagged packets and VLAN 20 never observed despite being required.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR has zero visibility into required VLAN 20 (50% of traffic). Cannot monitor east-west traffic or segment-specific threats on that VLAN, creating a complete blind spot and breaking detection coverage for that zone.

recommended_fix.why: Configure TAP/SPAN and packet broker ingress/egress ports as trunk with 802.1Q preservation enabled for VLANs 10 and 20, and disable any VLAN stripping/removal feature so NDR receives correctly tagged traffic.

findings.root_cause: 94.2% of bytes are TLS/encrypted, above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is not being decrypted before the tool, so payload is opaque. This is expected with modern TLS 1.2/1.3 but exceeds what this NDR can handle without a decryption feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for signature and behavioral analysis; with 94% encrypted it is limited to metadata/flow analysis only, sharply reducing detection of C2, exfiltration and exploit payloads and increasing false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Add selective TLS decryption/mirroring of decrypted copy via packet broker or TLS-intercept proxy for NDR-relevant flows, or feed enriched JA3/metadata from firewall/proxy, to restore payload visibility while respecting privacy/policy.
